The response is the only time you see `webhookSecret`. The test saves it as the `webhookSecret` variable (never logged). Set `webhookUrl` first: a public https address of your receiver.

operationId: createWatch

Create a watch as the signed-in user (email or webhook; no Turnstile). sourceUrl may be percia-cam://<cameraId> for one of your own phone or bridge cameras; a private address (192.168.x.x, an NVR) is refused: the person installs the Percia bridge (https://github.com/velvee-ai/percia-bridge) to push that camera. Send `goal`, or `agentId` (+ optional `agentVersion`; omitted = follow the latest) to deploy a published agent. Percia reads the goal through its intelligence layer (see POST /watches/draft). Send `draftId` (a ready draft from POST /watches/draft, with `acknowledgeUnsupported: true` when it left parts out) instead of `goal`; the draft holds the conditions. A create with a `goal` is read by Percia's layer first. A clear goal creates the watch as before. An unclear one creates nothing and answers 422 `clarification_needed` with `draftId`, `question` and `options` (and `guidance`): ask the person, answer with POST /watches/draft/{draftId}/answer {text}, then create with {sourceUrl, draftId}; or send a clearer goal. Parts that cannot be watched answer 409 `unsupported_not_acknowledged` (tell the person, then repeat with `acknowledgeUnsupported: true`). Per-watch tuning knobs from older versions are refused with 422 `invalid_request` naming the field in `error.field` (cooldownS, kind, rearmS, recheckS, minConfidence, notWhen, zones, concerns, judgeKey, interpret, runtime): the goal and the draft say everything.

Scopes: watches:write.
